data.title: Systemic lupus erythematosus — viva
data.summary: Connective tissue diseases · 14 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Systemic lupus erythematosus** (Connective tissue diseases)_

**Q1. Define SLE.**
- Chronic multisystem autoimmune disease with autoantibodies (especially to nuclear antigens) and immune-complex–mediated tissue injury of skin, joints, kidneys, serosa, blood, CNS; women of child-bearing age (F:M ~9:1)

**Q2. Pathogenesis.**
- Genetic (HLA-DR2/DR3, complement C1q/C2/C4 deficiency, TREX1, IRF5, STAT4) + environmental triggers (UV, drugs, EBV, oestrogen, smoking) → impaired clearance of apoptotic cells → exposure of nuclear antigens → loss of tolerance → autoantibodies → immune complexes deposit → complement activation and inflammation
- Type I interferon signature (plasmacytoid DCs) — basis for anifrolumab; B-cell hyperactivity (BAFF/BLyS — belimumab)

**Q3. Discuss the latest classification of SLE (PYQ).**
- 2019 EULAR/ACR criteria: entry criterion ANA ≥1:80 on HEp-2 cells (ever); then additive weighted criteria in 7 clinical and 3 immunological domains; classify as SLE with ≥10 points and ≥1 clinical criterion (each counted only highest in a domain)
- Clinical: constitutional (fever 2); haematological (leucopenia 3, thrombocytopenia 4, autoimmune haemolysis 4); neuropsychiatric (delirium 2, psychosis 3, seizure 5); mucocutaneous (non-scarring alopecia 2, oral ulcers 2, subacute cutaneous or discoid lupus 4, acute cutaneous lupus 6); serosal (effusion 5, acute pericarditis 6); musculoskeletal (joint involvement 6); renal (proteinuria >0.5 g/24 h 4, class II/V nephritis 8, class III/IV nephritis 10)
- Immunological: antiphospholipid antibodies 2; complement — low C3 or C4 3, low C3 and C4 4; SLE-specific antibodies — anti-dsDNA or anti-Smith 6
- Earlier: 1997 ACR (4 of 11) and 2012 SLICC (4 of 17 with ≥1 clinical and ≥1 immunological, or biopsy-proven lupus nephritis with ANA/anti-dsDNA)

**Q4. Describe the cutaneous manifestations of lupus (Gilliam classification — PYQ).**
- LE-specific: acute cutaneous LE (ACLE — malar 'butterfly' rash sparing nasolabial folds, generalised photosensitive eruption, TEN-like ACLE), subacute cutaneous LE (SCLE — annular/papulosquamous, anti-Ro, drug-induced), chronic cutaneous LE (CCLE — DLE, lupus profundus/panniculitis, chilblain lupus, lupus tumidus, hypertrophic/verrucous DLE, mucosal DLE, LP–LE overlap)
- LE-non-specific: vascular — Raynaud's, livedo reticularis, vasculitis (urticarial, leukocytoclastic), periungual telangiectasia, thrombophlebitis, Degos-like lesions; non-scarring alopecia (lupus hair — frontal broken hairs), oral ulcers (painless palatal), bullous SLE, calcinosis, rheumatoid nodules, sclerodactyly, erythema multiforme-like (Rowell's)
- Risk of SLE: ACLE ~100% association, SCLE ~50% meet criteria (mild), DLE ~5–10% (higher if widespread)

**Q5. Discuss the systemic manifestations (renal and cardiac — PYQ).**
- Constitutional: fever, fatigue, weight loss
- Musculoskeletal: non-erosive polyarthritis (Jaccoud's arthropathy — reducible deformities), avascular necrosis (steroids), myositis
- Renal (lupus nephritis, 40–60%) — ISN/RPS classes: I minimal mesangial, II mesangial proliferative, III focal (<50% glomeruli), IV diffuse (≥50% — most common and severe; 'wire loop' lesions), V membranous, VI advanced sclerosing; monitor urine protein, sediment, creatinine; biopsy if proteinuria >0.5 g/day
- Cardiac: pericarditis (commonest), myocarditis, Libman–Sacks (non-infective verrucous) endocarditis on mitral valve, premature atherosclerosis/CAD; congenital heart block in neonatal lupus (anti-Ro)
- Lungs: pleuritis/effusion, pneumonitis, alveolar haemorrhage, shrinking lung, pulmonary hypertension
- Haematological: anaemia (chronic disease, AIHA), leucopenia/lymphopenia, thrombocytopenia, APS
- Neuropsychiatric: seizures, psychosis, cognitive dysfunction, stroke, neuropathy
- GI: serositis, mesenteric vasculitis, hepatitis; eyes: retinal vasculitis (cytoid bodies), sicca

**Q6. Describe the various immunological tests (PYQ).**
- ANA by IIF on HEp-2 — most sensitive (>95%) screening; patterns: homogeneous (dsDNA, histone), speckled (Sm, RNP, Ro, La), nucleolar (scleroderma), centromere (limited SSc), rim/peripheral (dsDNA)
- Anti-dsDNA — specific (~95%); titre correlates with nephritis/activity
- Anti-Sm — most specific (~99%), low sensitivity
- Anti-histone — drug-induced lupus (>95%)
- Anti-Ro (SS-A)/La (SS-B) — SCLE, neonatal lupus, Sjögren's, ANA-negative lupus
- Anti-U1 RNP — MCTD
- Antiphospholipid: anticardiolipin, anti-β2 glycoprotein I, lupus anticoagulant
- Complements C3, C4 (low in active disease), CH50; anti-C1q (nephritis); Coombs test; ESR high with normal CRP (unless infection/serositis)

**Q7. Write a short note on the LE cell phenomenon (PYQ).**
- Neutrophil that has phagocytosed the denatured nuclear material (homogeneous haematoxylin body) of another cell opsonised by antinuclear (anti-histone/DNA) antibodies — described by Hargraves (1948)
- Positive in ~70–80% of SLE but also in drug-induced lupus, RA, hepatitis; now replaced by ANA/anti-dsDNA testing

**Q8. Write a short note on the lupus band test (PYQ).**
- DIF showing continuous granular band of immunoglobulins (IgG, IgM, ± IgA) and complement (C3) along the dermo-epidermal junction
- Lesional skin: positive in DLE (~70–90%) and SLE lesions
- Non-lesional skin: sun-protected (buttock/inner arm) positive in ~50% SLE (associated with nephritis and active disease); sun-exposed non-lesional positive in ~70–80% SLE
- False positives: rosacea, PMLE, normal sun-exposed skin (usually only IgM)

**Q9. What is the antiphospholipid syndrome? (lupus anticoagulant — PYQ)**
- Arterial/venous thrombosis and/or pregnancy morbidity (recurrent miscarriage <10 weeks, fetal death >10 weeks, pre-eclampsia/placental insufficiency) with persistently positive antiphospholipid antibodies (12 weeks apart)
- Lupus anticoagulant: paradoxically prolongs phospholipid-dependent clotting tests in vitro (aPTT, dilute Russell viper venom time) not corrected by mixing with normal plasma but corrected by adding excess phospholipid — but causes thrombosis in vivo
- Skin: livedo reticularis/racemosa, ulcers, necrosis, splinter haemorrhages, Degos-like lesions, anetoderma, catastrophic APS
- Treatment: warfarin (INR 2–3) for thrombosis; aspirin + LMWH in pregnancy

**Q10. How do you assess disease activity?**
- SLEDAI-2K, BILAG, ECLAM; CLASI for skin (activity and damage); SLICC/ACR damage index

**Q11. Management of SLE.**
- All: photoprotection, hydroxychloroquine 200–400 mg/day (≤5 mg/kg real body weight) for every patient unless contraindicated — reduces flares, damage, thrombosis; annual eye screening after 5 years (baseline)
- Mild (skin, joints): HCQ, NSAIDs, low-dose prednisolone, topical steroids/tacrolimus
- Moderate: prednisolone ≤7.5 mg/day long-term target, methotrexate, azathioprine, mycophenolate
- Severe organ (nephritis class III/IV, CNS): IV methylprednisolone pulses, mycophenolate or low-dose IV cyclophosphamide (Euro-Lupus), belimumab add-on, voclosporin, obinutuzumab
- Biologics: belimumab (anti-BLyS), anifrolumab (type I IFN receptor antibody — also good for skin), rituximab (off-label)
- Manage comorbidities: cardiovascular risk, bone health, infections (vaccines), APS anticoagulation, pregnancy planning (disease quiet ≥6 months; continue HCQ, aspirin)

**Q12. What is drug-induced lupus?**
- Classic: procainamide, hydralazine, isoniazid, minocycline, quinidine, methyldopa, TNF inhibitors, chlorpromazine; slow acetylators
- Features: arthralgia, serositis, fever; renal/CNS/skin rare; anti-histone antibodies; anti-dsDNA usually negative (except anti-TNF); resolves on withdrawal
- Drug-induced SCLE: terbinafine, hydrochlorothiazide, calcium channel blockers, PPIs, ACE inhibitors, taxanes, griseofulvin, anti-TNF — anti-Ro positive

**Q13. What is neonatal lupus?**
- Transplacental maternal anti-Ro/La antibodies → annular erythematous lesions (periorbital 'raccoon eyes'), photosensitive, resolves by 6 months; congenital heart block (permanent — needs pacing), hepatobiliary disease, cytopenias
- Mother may be asymptomatic; future pregnancies risk ~15–20%; HCQ during pregnancy reduces heart block risk

**Q14. Write a note on mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD — PYQ).**
- Overlap of SLE, SSc, polymyositis/DM features with high titre anti-U1 RNP antibodies
- Raynaud's (nearly all), puffy/swollen hands (sausage fingers), sclerodactyly, arthritis, myositis, oesophageal dysmotility, pulmonary hypertension (main cause of death); renal and CNS disease uncommon
- Treatment according to organ involvement; steroids responsive features (myositis, serositis)

## Quick spotter facts
- Malar rash sparing nasolabial folds — ACLE
- 2019 EULAR/ACR: ANA ≥1:80 entry + ≥10 points
- Anti-Sm most specific; anti-dsDNA tracks nephritis; anti-histone — drug lupus

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Lupus erythematosus); 2019 EULAR/ACR SLE classification criteria. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
